You offered to buy her the game so she could have her *own* space while still playing together online—a solution that respects both your autonomy and her desire for shared interaction. - **Her reaction is disproportionate.** Labeling you an "asshole baby" for wanting to personalize your own experience is immature. True "togetherness" in this context would mean collaborating *across* separate towns (e.g., visiting each other’s islands, trading items), not forcing one person to relinquish creative control. - **Technical reality:** Nintendo Switch games are tied to user profiles, not consoles. Sharing one console’s town means only one person can play at a time, and all decisions affect both players. With separate consoles, you can *both* enjoy your ideal towns while still playing together online—exactly what the game is built for. **Key takeaway:** You’re not being petty. You’re advocating for a healthy, mutually beneficial setup. Her insistence on a single town reflects a misunderstanding of how the game works, and her emotional reaction is unjustified. Prioritize your own enjoyment and boundaries—this isn’t selfish, it’s practical.
